thread:
olivia: FYI escalated from ACME — they're seeing TTFB p95/p99 regressions only on streaming responses. Non-stream (sync) endpoints look fine. Customer reports first-byte gaps of ~1.2s-3.5s intermittently. request_id: rq_0a1b2c3d.

olivia: Quick repro steps they gave: curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-v1-large\",\"prompt\":\"ping\"}' 
They say switching to non-stream removes the spike.

mike: thanks — can you paste a small HAR or a link to a trace? is this region-specific (us-west vs eu)? also ask if they use proxy/edge in front of our api.

olivia: attaching short log snippet from their side (redacted):
```
[2026-03-02T15:12:03Z] recv chunk 1 len=512
[2026-03-02T15:12:04Z] WAIT flush-window=200ms -> delayed by 1800ms
[2026-03-02T15:12:06Z] chunk 2 len=128
```
They say this pattern happens ~p99 when responses are multi-chunk. Region = us-west-2. They are on Dedicated.

xiang: sounds like chunk-coalescing at the proxy or edge is delaying flush. Could be our HTTP/2 multiplexer or an nginx keepalive/windowing issue. Any chance their app is reading slowly?

tara: we ruled out client-side backpressure — they tested with a simple netcat consumer and still saw gaps.

mike: ok. two quick triage actions: 1) request the routed trace (x-request-id -> full route) from our logs, 2) run a controlled repro against the same dedicated pool with `--no-coalesce` flag to the runtime. xiang do you have a small cmdline to toggle coalescing on runtime?

xiang: yes — we can enable `runtime.flush_window_ms=0` per-tenant for a test. I can push config to a single host in the dedicated pool. That will verify if runtime coalescing is the cause.

jen: create an incident? we should inform SRE and eng-runtime, and propose a temporary customer-specific mitigation (non-stream fallback) while we debug. also loop PM/AM. :eyes:

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-3476 by jen. Priority P1 -> P2 after initial triage. Assigned: eng-runtime, oncall-sre.

mike: also log shows occasional `proxy: flush_leader_sleep` messages around the same time. That points to edge aggregator delaying smaller chunks. I'll grep for those for the tenant id.

olivia: pasted the traced route: https://telemetry.redwood.ai/trace/rq_0a1b2c3d (internal) — shows hop at edge-proxy-5 where first-chunk emitted but next chunk delayed before reaching runtime.

xiang: interesting — edge-proxy appears to buffer until either a threshold or flush_timer. If we see larger gaps only on streaming, likely the aggregator coalescing policy (for HTTP/2 header compression or conn reuse) is aggressive. Two mitigations: 1) lower edge flush window to 50ms for that tenant, 2) enable tenant-specific non-stream fallback in the gateway so the client can use sync until fix. Option 2 is lowest risk.

tara: customer prefers no change in client code, so gateway fallback is ideal (we transparently return non-stream). they'll accept short degraded latency but no spikes.

jen: can we do a quick canary: enable gateway-fallback for that tenant and monitor p95 for 30min? if stable, roll to other affected tenants. I'll draft a customer note.

mike: one more ask — gather server-side per-chunk timing: emit KV pairs `chunk_emit_ts` and `chunk_sent_ts` to correlate runtime vs edge. xiang can enable at debug level for 1 host.

xiang: will do. pushing `flush_window_ms=0` to host runtime-07 in dedicated pool and enabling per-chunk debug for 10 minutes.

ops-bot: Change applied by xiang on runtime-07. Change-id CHG-8812.

olivia: customer confirmed gateway fallback reduced TTFB spikes immediately in test. p99 dropped from ~6.1s to ~0.9s for streaming fallback to non-stream.

jen: action items:
- olivia: confirm customer acceptance and schedule follow-up call (owner)
- xiang: collect debug traces and revert runtime debug after capture (owner)
- mike: audit edge-proxy coalescing config and propose long-term fix (owner)
- eng-runtime: evaluate smarter flush heuristics (e.g., first-chunk no-coalesce)
- support: prepare KB entry on tenant fallback for streaming spikes

olivia: I'll send the customer note and mark this thread with INC-2026-3476. thanks everyone. :heart:
